findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

I found no errors in recovery-plan.md or proof-map.md, so I'm approving. Both files present themselves as planning and research material only. They claim no RED, no certification and no completion authority, which matches delivery-state.md, the CKWE2D-only restriction in retrospective-history-core.ts, and the spec's split of ownership. Every count I could check agrees with proof-inventory.json: - 14 blocks and 37 cases (per-block counts 1/4/1/3/2/2/1/6/6/3/3/3/1/1). - 11 Vitest files. - 42 unchecked R/G/R entries plus one cross-scenario entry. - 33 deferrals by owner: DRD65E 1, KKP2R3 2, MCWV4B 18, FC33HK 12. Each block's preserved limit matches the accepted limits in delivery-state.md. The plan names the main risks and assigns each one to a future recovery feature rather than leaving it to implementation: stale authority imported from #5857, swapping historical identities, a whole-ticket lifecycle exemption, and same-agent certification. My findings are warnings and notes, not blockers.

proof-map.md 'Historical protection' cites figures that nothing in the packet supports: 'six failures', '585 unfinished checks', the GREEN/REFACTOR SHA collision, and three DRD65E/KKP2R3 cases with 'no original ledger heading'. The inventory only hashes the 5F5ZZA ledger; it does not itemize these. Add these figures to proof-inventory.json or cite their source, so the later reconciliation review can check them instead of inheriting them as trusted text.

recovery-plan.md §1 hands the case-to-assertion mapping for parameterized proofs to the future feature. Three blocks rest on a single templated title: Retained reuse (6 cases → '$label'), Corrupt retained output (6 → '$label') and Refused selectors (2 → '%s'). proof-map.md calls out the order of fallback attempts and route admission specifically, but not these. Name them explicitly as rows that need row-level mapping, so a test that passes by title alone can't count as covering all 14 cases.

In recovery-plan.md §1, the ticket.md projection binds identity, scope, out_of_scope, done_when and parent linkage, but leaves status and phase outside the bound projection. A closing transition that rewrites status or phase could therefore change which planning stages count as satisfied, and this is the problem §4 says must be specified before completion is enabled. Make sure the future contract treats phase changes as gated transitions, not as ordinary lifecycle noise.

The plan says root Cucumber acceptance excludes `@proof.vitest` and that #5857's baseline is not an ancestor of main. Nothing in the supplied context can confirm either claim. They aren't load-bearing for the planning deliverable, but the implementation should re-check them before relying on them.

The inventory step text 'containing a failed observation conformance records for an exact reviewer identity' reads like an artifact of the outline substitution. The note that the inventory is 'research input, never a trusted receipt' covers this, but the reconciliation should record the actual compiled step bytes, not this prose.
